title: Wooden Joe Nicholas as a trumpeter
summary: He played with Wooden Joe in the Camellia band; Joe used ordinary mutes, played softly, but not mutes on parades.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Do you remember Wooden Joe Nicholas? Oh yeah, I remember Wooden Joe. Did he play with the Camellia Band?
Yeah, that's right. He was a trumpet player, played with the Camellia Band. I thought he was with him. That's right. When you were with him? I played with him. Yeah, I was with him.
How was Wooden Joe the trumpet player?
Oh, he's a fine trumpet player. Did he use mutes too? Yeah, I was with Joe reading music, I'm sure he did.
I mean, did he use those mutes like you were saying, McCary? Did he use any?
No, no, he used ordinary mutes and all that.
Just straight ordinary mutes? Yeah. But he did use mutes?
Yeah, he used mutes, yeah. The practically average trumpet player used mutes around at that time.
Did he ever play soft Wooden Joe?
Play softly? Yes, soft trumpet player. He could play choir. Yeah, choir trumpet player. Played clarinet too. Well, that's Alfred Nicholas, his uncle.
Did he play both his clarinet and his clarinet?
No, no. I don't recall him playing clarinet. I know he could play clarinet. He played trumpet.
He played parades too, didn't he? Parades too, correct. How was he as a parade trumpeter? Well, he's fine. Did he ever use mutes on a parade?
No, no mutes on a parade.
Did he blow loud in a parade?
Would you say was there any special loudness or anything?
